questions.title: Count in a Sorted Array
questions.description:
A duplicate scanner counts how many times a value appears in a sorted array — combine the first- and last-occurrence binary searches instead of scanning. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int countInSorted(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the number of occurrences of target (0 when absent).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the occurrence count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Closest Element
questions.description:
A thermostat finds the calibration value closest to a target in a sorted list. On a distance tie the SMALLER element wins. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int closestElement(int[] arr, int target)

arr is sorted ascending (distinct values). It must return the element minimising |element - target|; ties go to the smaller element.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the closest element.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Linear Search Index
questions.description:
The most basic search: walk the array from the left and report where the target first appears. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int linearSearch(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the first index of target, or -1 when it is absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Binary Search Index
questions.description:
Search a sorted array by halving the range. The array is sorted in ascending order and has distinct values. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int binarySearch(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the index of target, or -1 when it is absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Count Occurrences (Unsorted)
questions.description:
Count how many times a value appears in an unsorted array — only a linear scan can help. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int countOccurrences(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the number of elements equal to target.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Index of the Maximum
questions.description:
A linear-search relative: find WHERE the largest value sits. Report the index of its FIRST occurrence. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int maxIndex(int[] arr)

It must return the smallest index holding the maximum value.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the index of the first maximum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: First Occurrence (Sorted)
questions.description:
In a sorted array with duplicates, binary search must still land on the LEFTMOST matching index. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int firstOccurrence(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the leftmost index of target, or -1 when absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the first index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Last Occurrence (Sorted)
questions.description:
The twin of first occurrence: in a sorted array with duplicates, find the RIGHTMOST matching index. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int lastOccurrence(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the rightmost index of target, or -1 when absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the last index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Library Book Lookup
questions.description:
A librarian scans shelf IDs one by one for a requested book. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int findBook(int[] ids, int target)

It must return the shelf position (0-based index) of the target ID, or -1 when the book is missing.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated shelf IDs. Line 3: the requested ID.

Output Format:
One line with the position or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= id, target <= 100000

questions.title: Exam Roll Number Finder
questions.description:
Results are published with roll numbers sorted ascending; the office uses binary search. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int findRoll(int[] rolls, int target)

It must return the index of the roll number in the sorted list, or -1 when absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct roll numbers. Line 3: the queried roll number.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000, 1 <= roll, target <= 100000

questions.title: Sorted or Not
questions.description:
Binary search only works on sorted data. A pre-check verifies that an array is non-decreasing. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isSorted(int[] arr)

It must return 1 when every arr[i] <= arr[i + 1], and 0 otherwise.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: First Price Above Budget
questions.description:
A shopper scans a sorted price list for the first item they cannot afford. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int firstAbove(int[] prices, int budget)

It must return the index of the first price strictly greater than budget, or -1 when every price fits the budget.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted prices. Line 3: the budget.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000, 1 <= price, budget <= 100000

questions.title: Search Insert Position
questions.description:
A scheduler inserts an appointment into a sorted distinct list and needs the index where it belongs (the first index whose value is >= target, or n when the target is the largest). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int searchInsert(int[] arr, int target)

arr is sorted ascending with distinct values; target is guaranteed absent. Return the insert index.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the insert index.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Upper Bound Index
questions.description:
A price engine asks for the UPPER BOUND: the first index whose value is strictly greater than the query (n when none is). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int upperBound(int[] arr, int target)

arr is sorted ascending. It must return the first index i with arr[i] > target, or arr.length when none exists.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the upper-bound index.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Integer Square Root by Search
questions.description:
A scaling library computes floor(sqrt(n)) WITHOUT floating point — binary search on the answer space [0, 2000000000]. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long intSqrt(long n)

It must return the largest r with r * r <= n. Compare with division (mid <= n / mid) so the squares cannot overflow.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with floor of the square root.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000000000000

questions.title: Minimum in a Rotated List
questions.description:
A nightly job rotates a sorted report k positions; the morning shift needs the minimum value of the rotated array. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int findMin(int[] arr)

arr is an ascending distinct array rotated by some amount. It must return the minimum element — binary search against arr[hi].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (rotated ascending, distinct).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Missing Roll Number
questions.description:
A sorted register holds every roll number from 0 to n except one, which went missing. Because the register is sorted, arr[i] equals i until the gap — binary search finds it. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int missingNumber(int[] arr)

arr is sorted ascending, distinct, holding n values from the range [0, n] with exactly one missing. It must return the missing number.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (the register without its missing number).

Output Format:
One line with the missing number.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Bitonic Peak Finder
questions.description:
A hiking log first climbs and then descends: values strictly increase up to the summit, then strictly decrease. Locate the summit index with binary search. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int findPeak(int[] arr)

arr is strictly increasing then strictly decreasing (length >= 3, summit strictly inside). It must return the index of the maximum.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (bitonic).

Output Format:
One line with the summit index.

Constraints:
3 <= n <= 100000, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Search a Rotated Array
questions.description:
The rotated report from the morning shift now needs a full search: find a target in a rotated ascending distinct array. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int rotatedSearch(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the index of target, or -1 when absent. Decide which half is sorted at every step.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (rotated ascending, distinct). Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Kth Smallest Across Two Lists
questions.description:
Two sorted scoreboards must be queried for the k-th smallest score OVERALL — without merging everything. Walk both lists, always advancing the smaller front, and stop at the k-th pick (left wins ties). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int kthSmallest(int[] a, int[] b, int k)

a and b are sorted ascending; k is 1-based and never exceeds a.length + b.length.

Input Format:
Line 1: n and m. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: m sorted integers. Line 4: k.

Output Format:
One line with the k-th smallest value overall.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 5000, 1 <= k <= n + m, -1000 <= value <= 1000
